# Setup

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(conflicted)
library(tidyverse)
library(tidybayes)
library(distributional)
library(brms)
library(ggdist)
library(bayesplot)
library(patchwork)

source("functions.R")

conflicts_prefer(dplyr::filter,
                 stats::lag,
                 distributional::parameters,
                 brms::ar,
                 brms::dstudent_t,
                 brms::pstudent_t,
                 brms::qstudent_t,
                 brms::rstudent_t,
                 brms::rhat)

options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())
options(brms.file_refit = "on_change")
options(brms.backend = "cmdstanr")
options(contrasts = c("contr.sum", "contr.poly"))

options(digits = 3)

set.seed(2058)

if (!dir.exists("fits/cwm")) dir.create("fits/cwm", recursive = T)

theme_set(theme_minimal())

cwm_ITP <- readRDS("intermediate/cwm_itp.rds")

show <- vars(!c(lprior, lp__, b_Intercept))
```

```{r}
#this emulates ppc_dens_overlay but weighs observations and predictions by cover
my_ppc <- function(fit, data, weight = "cov_wt", range = T){
  resp <- fit[["formula"]][["resp"]]
  
  #if data comes from multiple imputations, average across them
  if(is.data.frame(data[[1]])){
    data <- data |>
      map(\(x) x |> 
            mutate(id = row_number())) |> 
      bind_rows() |> 
      summarise(across(everything(), \(x) if(is.numeric(x)) mean(x) else first(x)), .by = id) |> 
      mutate(cov_wt = cov_wt / sum(cov_wt),
             site = fct_drop(site))
  }
  
  preds <- predicted_draws(fit, data, ndraws = 10)
  
  plot <- preds |> 
    ggplot(aes(y = after_stat(wdensity), weight = .data[[weight]])) +
    geom_density(aes(x = .prediction, group = .draw), colour = alpha("#005b96", 0.25)) +
    geom_density(aes(x = .data[[resp]]), data = data)
  
  if(range){
    plot +
      coord_cartesian(xlim = range(data[[resp]]))
  } else plot
}

my_resplot <- function(fit, data, ndraws = 500){
  fit |> 
    residual_draws(data |> 
                     mutate(site = fct_drop(site)),
                   ndraws = ndraws) |> 
    as_tibble() |> 
    ggplot(aes(x = .row, y = .residual, alpha = cov_wt)) +
    stat_pointinterval(.width = 0.95, show.legend = F)
}
```

# Priors 

## Gaussian

See the previous notebooks for more information about prior choice.

## Lognormal

For a log-normal distribution, the two independent parameters are median $exp(u)$ and CV $\sqrt{exp(\sigma^{2})-1}$.

```{r}
expand_grid(meanlog = seq(-1, 2, by = 0.5),
            sdlog = c(0.1, 0.5, 1),
            seq = seq(from = 0, to = 20, length.out = 400)) |> 
  mutate(d   = dlnorm(seq, meanlog, sdlog),
         mu  = str_c("mu[log]==", meanlog),
         sigma = str_c("sigma[log]==", sdlog)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = seq, y = d)) +
  geom_area(fill = "grey50") +
  scale_y_continuous("density", breaks = NULL) +
  ggtitle(expression("Log-normal given different combinations of "*mu[log]*" and "*sigma[log])) +
  facet_grid(mu ~ sigma, labeller = label_parsed, scales = "free")
```

We can see that the default prior, with the predictors at their means, the median value is likely change over more than four orders of magnitude (for scaled traits). This is far too wide.

```{r}
tibble(x = rstudent_t(1e4, 3, 0, 2.5)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = x)) +
  stat_halfeye(fill = "brown") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = \(x) str_c("\u00d7", signif(exp(x), 2)),
                     limits = c(-10, 10)) +
  labs(title = "Default prior for Intercept",
       x = "Median",
       y = NULL)
```

The adjusted prior is still wide but more reasonable.

```{r}
tibble(x = rstudent_t(1e4, 3, 0, 0.6)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = x)) +
  stat_halfeye(fill = "slategray3") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = \(x) str_c("\u00d7", signif(exp(x), 2)),
                     limits = c(-4, 4)) +
  labs(title = "Adjusted prior for Intercept",
       x = "Median",
       y = NULL)
```

Here's the proposed prior for $\beta$ in relative terms:

```{r}
tibble(x = rstudent_t(1e4, 5, 0, 0.5)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = x)) +
  stat_halfeye(fill = "lightsalmon") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = \(x) str_c("\u00d7", signif(exp(x), 2)),
                     limits = c(-3, 3),
                     breaks = -3:3) +
  labs(title = expression("Adjusted prior for"~beta),
       x = "Difference in medians",
       y = NULL)
```

And for $\sigma$:

```{r}
tibble(r = generate(dist_truncated(dist_student_t(5, 0, 0.5), 0), 1e4)[[1]],
       x = sqrt(exp(r^2) - 1)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = x)) +
  stat_halfeye(fill = "khaki3") +
  xlim(NA, 6) +
  labs(title = "Prior for sigma in terms of CV",
       x = "CV")
```

## Store the priors

The following function emulates the default behaviour of `brms` for the intercept prior, using the outcome median as mean, but using the adjusted df and sd.

```{r}
#prior for gaussian models
prior_itp <- c(prior(normal(0, 1), class = "b"),
               prior(student_t(3, 0, 0.7), class = "b", coef = "site1"),
               prior(student_t(3, 0, 0.7), class = "b", coef = "site2"),
               prior(student_t(3, 0, 0.5), class = "sigma", lb = 0))

#prior for lognormal models
prior_ln <- function(outcome, hu = F){
  md <- outcome |> median() |> log() |> round(3)
  prior <- c(set_prior(str_c("student_t(3, ", md, ", 0.6)"), class = "Intercept"),
             prior(student_t(5, 0, 0.5), class = "b"),
             prior(student_t(5, 0, 0.5), class = "sigma", lb = 0))
  
  if(hu) prior <- c(prior, prior(normal(0,1), class = "b", dpar = "hu"))
  return(prior)
}
```

## Prior predictive simulation

```{r}
data_prior <- tibble(x = seq(-2, 2, length.out = 10),
                     cover = seq(0, 4, length.out = 10)) |>
  expand_grid(outcome = c(0, 1),
              z = seq(-2, 2, length.out = 10),
              site = letters[1:4])

prior_pred <- brm(bf(outcome ~ x + z + x:z + cover + site,
                     hu ~ x + z + x:z + cover + site),
             data = data_prior,
             prior = prior_ln(data_prior$outcome, hu = T),
             sample_prior = "only",
             family = "hurdle_lognormal",
             file = "fits/prior_h_ln",
             seed = 2853)

#lognormal model
prior_pred |> 
  spread_draws(Intercept, b_site1, sigma) |> 
  slice_sample(n = 100) |> 
  mutate(site1 = Intercept + b_site1) |> 
  pivot_longer(c(Intercept, site1)) |> 
  expand_grid(x = seq(0, 10, length.out = 100)) |> 
  mutate(density = dlnorm(x, value, sigma)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = density, group = .draw)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.2) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 10)) +
  facet_wrap(vars(name))

#hurdle model
prior_pred |> 
  spread_draws(Intercept_hu, b_hu_site1) |> 
  mutate(site1 = Intercept_hu + b_hu_site1) |> 
  pivot_longer(c(Intercept_hu, site1)) |>
  mutate(value = plogis(value)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = value)) +
  geom_density(fill = "grey40") +
  facet_wrap(vars(name))
```

# Years included in the models

The years considered across all models are:

```{r}
years_across <- cwm_ITP$data |> 
  map(1) |> 
  bind_rows() |> 
  distinct(year) |> 
  mutate(year = as.character(year)) |> 
  arrange(year) |> 
  pull()

years_across
```

This corresponds to a timespan of `{r} as.numeric(years_across) |> range() |> diff() |> sum(1)` years.

The years included are the same for all models:

```{r}
cwm_ITP |> 
  mutate(years_diff = map_dbl(data,
                              \(x) x |> 
                                pluck(1) |> 
                                distinct(year) |> 
                                mutate(year = as.character(year)) |> 
                                pull() |> 
                                setdiff(years_across) |> 
                                length())) |> 
  select(!data)
```

while the number of site-years differs because of different trait filtering

```{r}
cwm_ITP |> 
  mutate(site_years = map_dbl(data,
                              \(x) x |> 
                                pluck(1) |> 
                                distinct(site, year) |> 
                                nrow())) |> 
  select(!data)
```

# Prepare data

```{r}
variables <- c("air_t_mean", "soil_t_mean", "precipitation")

sds <- c(2.5, 2.5, 600) |> 
  set_names(variables)

prepare <- function(data, out, vars = variables) {
  
  #some processing is applied to both exposure and outcome
  full_var <- c(out, vars)
  
  # SD for the outcome
  sds <- data[[1]] |> 
    summarise(sd_out = sd(.data[[out]])) |> 
    pull(sd_out) |> 
    set_names(out) |> 
    c(sds)
  
  data |> 
    map(\(x) {
      x |> 
        mutate(across(all_of(full_var), 
                      \(x) sds[[cur_column()]], 
                      .names = "{.col}_sd"),
               across(all_of(full_var), 
                      \(x) x / sds[[cur_column()]]),
               #cover as proportion 0-4
               cover = cover / 100 * 4) |> 
        # calculate site grand means
        mutate(across(all_of(vars), mean, 
                      .names = "{.col}_site"),
               across(all_of(vars),
                      \(x) x - get(str_c(cur_column(), "_site")),
                      .names = "{.col}_centered"),
               .by = site)
    })
}

cwm_ITP <- cwm_ITP |> 
  mutate(data = map2(data, trait, prepare) |> 
           set_names(trait))
```

# Sub-canopy weather

## Leaf area

```{r}
fit_la_itp <- brm_multiple(la | weights(cov_wt, scale = TRUE) ~ 
                             air_t_mean_centered + precipitation_centered +
                             air_t_mean_centered:precipitation_centered + cover + site,
                           data = cwm_ITP$data$la,
                           prior = prior_ln(cwm_ITP$data$la[[1]]$la),
                           family = "lognormal",
                           file = "fits/cwm/la.itp",
                           file_refit = "never",
                           control = list(seed = 2853))

prior_summary(fit_la_itp)

fit_la_itp

multiple_convergence(fit_la_itp)

my_mcmc_pairs(fit_la_itp)

trank(fit_la_itp)

my_ppc(fit_la_itp, cwm_ITP$data$la)

my_resplot(fit_la_itp, cwm_ITP$data$la[[1]])

mcmc_intervals(fit_la_itp, pars = show)

my_ceffects(fit_la_itp)
```

## Stem-specific density

*Ilex aquifolium* and *Ruscus aculeatus* have clearly higher SSD than the rest. While they are woody shrubs, there are other shrubs and woody species with lower values, so this doesn't fully account for the differences.

```{r}
fit_ssd_itp <- brm_multiple(ssd | weights(cov_wt, scale = TRUE) ~ 
                              air_t_mean_centered + precipitation_centered +

                            prior = prior_itp,
```

## Bud Bank (incl. root)

While this clonal trait is in principle a discrete count (bud in BB organs per rooting unit), its averaging across measurements and datasets results in a variable which is more similar to continuous. This supports the use of Gaussian models, because the outcome is not a discrete count.
Similar considerations apply to multiplication rate and persistence.


## Persistence

According to CLO-PLA "the data are effectively truncated by the value of 4 years, which should be interpreted as 4 years or more". To correctly account for this in the model, persistence values of 4 are considered as right-censored. In practice, the results are substantially unaffected.

```{r}
fit_pers_itp <- brm_multiple(bf(persistence | weights(cov_wt, scale = TRUE) +
                                  cens(censored) ~
                                  soil_t_mean_centered + precipitation_centered +
                                  soil_t_mean_centered:precipitation_centered + cover + site,
                                hu ~ soil_t_mean_centered + precipitation_centered +
                                  soil_t_mean_centered:precipitation_centered + cover + site),
                             data = cwm_ITP$data$persistence |>
                               map(\(x) x |> 
                                     mutate(censored = if_else(persistence * persistence_sd == 4, 1, 0))),
                             prior = prior_ln(cwm_ITP$data$persistence[[1]]$persistence, hu = T),
                             family = "hurdle_lognormal",
                             file = "fits/cwm/persistence.itp",
                             file_refit = "never",
                             init = 0,
                             control = list(seed = 2853))

prior_summary(fit_pers_itp)

fit_pers_itp

multiple_convergence(fit_pers_itp)

my_mcmc_pairs(fit_pers_itp, vars(!contains(c("hu", "lp", "b_Intercept"))))

my_mcmc_pairs(fit_pers_itp, pars = vars(contains("hu")))

trank(fit_pers_itp)

my_ppc(fit_pers_itp, cwm_ITP$data$persistence, range = F)

#this plot may not be meaningful for censored models
my_resplot(fit_pers_itp, cwm_ITP$data$persistence[[1]])

mcmc_intervals(fit_pers_itp, pars = vars(!contains(c("hu", "lp", "b_Intercept"))))

mcmc_intervals(fit_pers_itp, pars = vars(contains("hu")))

my_ceffects(fit_pers_itp, hurdle = T)
```

# Store fits

```{r}
#load brms fits
fits <- list.files("fits/cwm", pattern = "\\.rds$", full.names = T) |> 
  map(readRDS) |> 
  as_tibble_col(column_name = "fit")

#organize the models
fits <- fits |> 
  mutate(name = list.files("fits/cwm", pattern = "\\.rds$") |> 
           str_remove("\\.rds$") |> 
           str_replace_all("\\.", "_"),
  trait = word(name, 1, sep = "_"),
  type = word(name, 2, sep = "_"))

#add data
fits <- fits |> 
  left_join(cwm_ITP) |> 
  #average across imputations
  mutate(data = map(data,
                    \(x) x |> map(\(t) t |> 
                             mutate(obs_id = row_number())) |>
                         bind_rows(.id = "imp") |> 
                         summarise(across(where(is.numeric), mean),
                                   .by = c(site, obs_id)) |> 
                         select(!obs_id)))
```

# Diagnostics

## Check number of divergent transitions

```{r}
fits <- fits |> 
    mutate(n_divergent = map_int(fit, 
                   \(x) nuts_params(x) |> 
                     filter(Parameter == "divergent__" & Value == 1) |> 
                     nrow()))

fits |> 
  select(!c(data, fit)) |> 
  filter(n_divergent > 0)
```

## Pareto *k*

In a weighted regression, the Pareto *k* diagnostic can flag points as influential just because their weight is large, so it is not computed here.

# Save results

```{r}
fits |> 
  select(!n_divergent) |> 
  saveRDS("intermediate/fits_cwm.rds")
```
